valid_fixes: Change FunctionUrlAuthType from AWS_IAM to NONE in the IngestFunctionUrlPermission resource in faulted.yaml
invalid_patches: Modifying the IngestFunction handler code — the fault is in the permission resource, not the handler
Changing the IngestFunctionUrl AuthType property instead of the Permission resource's FunctionUrlAuthType
Adding IAM credentials to the caller — the endpoint should be publicly accessible without authentication
optimal_diagnostic_path: ace_invoke_lambda(FunctionName=IngestFunction, Payload={body: '{"title": "test"}'}) → returns 200 — Lambda itself is fine
ace_invoke_endpoint(url=<IngestFunctionUrl>) → returns 403 Forbidden — the function URL rejects unauthenticated callers
Read faulted.yaml → IngestFunctionUrlPermission.FunctionUrlAuthType is AWS_IAM instead of NONE, requiring IAM SigV4 signatures on all requests
observable_symptom: Every POST to the ingest function URL returns HTTP 403 Forbidden. Direct Lambda invocation succeeds. The function URL is reachable but requires AWS IAM SigV4 request signing, so unsigned public callers are rejected.
root_cause: IngestFunctionUrlPermission.FunctionUrlAuthType is set to AWS_IAM instead of NONE. This overrides the permission grant so that the function URL requires callers to sign requests with valid AWS credentials. Public unsigned requests are rejected with 403 before the handler is ever invoked.
